The finding is factually accurate about this diff. records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — TopicEmbed.import's regex accepts `http://` while TopicRetriever rejects it via URI.host, so direct feed and Disqus callers can persist embeds under a different URL contract.
records.rationale: The finding describes no actual defect. TopicEmbed.import's regex `/^https?\:\/\//` accepting http:// URLs is intentional and harmless — feed items on http:// hosts are legitimately imported. TopicRetriever's `invalid_host?` check (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`) only governs whether the retriever fetches a remote URL, a different code path serving a different purpose. Nothing in the diff shows the two contracts producing broken behavior, data loss, or inconsistency; the claim of a 'different URL contract' causing a problem is speculative with no concrete mechanism.

records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — RSS content is stored as unsanitized raw HTML, allowing feed-supplied scripts or event handlers to execute in the forum origin.
records.rationale: Diff confirms the mechanism: Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, TopicEmbed.import creates posts from feed/remote content (RSS `i.content` or readability-extracted doc.content) with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and no sanitization is applied anywhere in the new code; best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. So feed-supplied scripts/event handlers would execute in the forum origin.

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Reusing the scheduled PollFeed job as a synchronous retriever couples cache-miss handling to job lifecycle, so later scheduling changes can silently change request-time importing.
records.rationale: The diff at lib/topic_retriever.rb line 41 shows `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` — the scheduled hourly job (declared with `recurrence { hourly }` and `sidekiq_options retry: false` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) is being invoked synchronously inside request-time retrieval. This is a real, specific coupling: PollFeed was designed as a scheduled job, yet perform_retrieve depends on running it inline, so changes to its schedule or sidekiq options would silently alter embed import behavior. Not a correctness defect in the current code (it works), so not a bug; it is a concrete architecture/
